tasks.title: Specify weighted rules, deterministic ties and live configuration replacement.
acceptance: Weight 3 beats two matching weight-1 rules.
Equal scores choose declaration order, even when alphabetical order differs.
A single positive score qualifies; zero evidence remains unknown.
Replacing the public configuration between calls immediately changes the result.
tasks.contract: Public codelang_detect.detect(text) uses codelang_detect.detector.PATTERNS, an insertion-ordered dict of output_label -> list[(compiled regex, positive integer weight)]. Each matching rule contributes once. The greatest strictly positive total wins; tied positive totals choose the first declared key. Read PATTERNS at call time; custom keys are valid output labels. No score means unknown.
tasks.rationale: The fixtures separate weighted scoring from match counting and declaration order from alphabetical order. Replacing the mapping between calls detects stale cached configuration; positive and zero-score controls distinguish an extra confidence threshold.

tasks.title: Specify CLI input routes and exact successful output.
acceptance: A Python snippet inside a .txt file is identified from its contents.
Piped text is accepted when no file argument exists.
Successful output has exactly one label/newline and no stderr.
tasks.contract: codelang_detect.cli.main() reads sys.argv and an optional UTF-8 file or sys.stdin. It detects content rather than suffix and prints exactly one lowercase label plus newline, with empty stderr on success. The starter detector recognizes clear Python as py and JavaScript as js. File-open failure raises SystemExit(2), stderr mentions "can't open", stdout is empty. Read/decoding/closed-stdin failures raise SystemExit(1), stderr starts "Error: Could not process the input.", stdout is empty, and normal input failures produce no traceback. Application runtime uses only the standard library.
tasks.rationale: A Python snippet stored as snippet.txt exposes filename-based guessing. Capturing stdout and stderr detects extra output, while the stdin fixture checks the other supported input route without touching the real console.

tasks.title: Specify CLI failure classes and useful diagnostics.
acceptance: Missing files produce usage exit 2 with useful stderr and empty stdout.
Closed stdin and invalid UTF-8 produce processing exit 1.
Normal input errors do not print tracebacks.
tasks.contract: codelang_detect.cli.main() reads sys.argv and an optional UTF-8 file or sys.stdin. It detects content rather than suffix and prints exactly one lowercase label plus newline, with empty stderr on success. The starter detector recognizes clear Python as py and JavaScript as js. File-open failure raises SystemExit(2), stderr mentions "can't open", stdout is empty. Read/decoding/closed-stdin failures raise SystemExit(1), stderr starts "Error: Could not process the input.", stdout is empty, and normal input failures produce no traceback. Application runtime uses only the standard library.
tasks.rationale: Missing files are usage failures, while decoding and closed-stream errors are processing failures. Exact exit codes and empty stdout prevent an implementation from treating every error as success; the traceback check also catches deliberately printed tracebacks.

tasks.title: Specify cumulative-return mathematics, missing values and input preservation.
acceptance: 100,150,75 yields 0,.5,-.25, not daily changes.
Different series can have different first-observed dates.
Missing observations and entirely missing columns stay missing.
Dates and input values are preserved; nonpositive baselines are rejected.
tasks.contract: Public coin_comparator.calculate_cumulative_returns(prices: pandas.DataFrame) returns price/first-observed-nonmissing-price minus 1 independently per column. Preserve row/column order, dates, missing observations and input values. An entirely missing series stays missing. Nonpositive observed baselines raise ValueError mentioning baseline. Do not forward fill or convert cumulative returns to daily changes.
tasks.rationale: The three-point path separates cumulative from daily returns. Different first-observed rows prevent using a shared first row; explicit NaNs prevent forward filling. Input comparison checks preservation, and positive-valued examples prevent an always-error implementation from passing.

tasks.contract: Public price_workflow.analyze(tickers,start,end,provider=None,csv_path=None) returns {returns:DataFrame,correlation:DataFrame,omitted:list[str],source:"csv"|"provider",observed_start:YYYY-MM-DD,observed_end:YYYY-MM-DD}. Normalize names to uppercase -USD; dates use [start,end). provider(symbols,start,end) returns a price frame. CSV uses a date index and named ticker columns, with no provider call. CSV/provider results match except inferred pandas frequency metadata. Omit and report only all-missing series; each retained series uses its first nonmissing positive baseline and preserves gaps. Empty selection or reversed dates raises ValueError before fetching. Nonpositive baselines raise ValueError mentioning baseline. Provider RuntimeError propagates for display; never fabricate zeros. The correlation matrix uses price values, not returns. Browser integration remains outside this task.

The provider spy checks normalized symbols; omitted-series and leading-gap controls protect the baseline policy. Errors must remain explicit instead of becoming zero-return results.
